q: In the rubber-hand illusion, what helps a visible fake hand start to feel like part of your own body?
Vibrating an arm tendon while a person holds their own nose can create which bizarre sensation?
In Aristotle’s touch illusion, one small object touching crossed fingertips can seem like what?
A thermal grill combines harmless warm and cool bars under the hand. What surprising sensation can the combination produce?
Two objects weigh exactly the same, but one is much smaller. In the classic size–weight illusion, which generally feels heavier?
In the “cutaneous rabbit” illusion, taps at separated points on the skin can seem to do what?
After pushing an arm outward against an immovable support, what odd movement can occur when the person relaxes?
You glance quickly at a clock and its second hand seems frozen for an unusually long moment. What has apparently stretched?
Researchers made completely dry surfaces feel damp in a moisture-free chamber. Which property did they vary?
Cambridge’s wearable robotic “Third Thumb” is strapped beside the hand. Which body parts control it through pressure sensors?
Durham researchers trained both blind and sighted adults to judge objects without vision by listening to echoes of what?
A 20-person listening study found that a difficult podcast task activated vestigial muscles normally associated with moving what?
In a lightproof room, a 2009 experiment’s ultrasensitive camera recorded a faint spontaneous glow from which unlit subjects?
In grip experiments, water-wrinkled fingertips let people use less force to hold which objects securely than smooth wet fingertips did?
A sensitive microphone in an ear canal can detect faint sounds generated by what unexpected source?
To test human scent-tracking, Berkeley researchers had blindfolded volunteers crawl along a grassy trail smelling of what?
In a GPS-tracked study, people trying to walk straight without a reliable directional cue often followed what unexpected paths?
In robot-mediated self-tickling experiments, what alteration made a person’s own touch feel more ticklish?
In a visual-imagination experiment, vividly picturing a bright shape could cause which real bodily response even without extra light?
In a 2021 study, some people answered simple questions while still lucid dreaming. How did they send replies to the researchers?
When a familiar sign was “on the tip of the fingers,” which part of its form was least readily recalled in a study of deaf signers?
In people blind from birth, research has found that spoken language can recruit brain regions usually associated with which other ability?
In the nasal cycle, what changes inside the nose to let airflow dominance shift between the nostrils?
A face photograph has its eyes and mouth flipped within the face. Which change can make the grotesque alteration much harder to notice?
In the McCollough illusion, black-and-white striped patterns can acquire apparent colors linked to which feature?
In a famous attention experiment, people counting basketball passes often missed someone walking through the scene dressed as what?
During a real-world conversation experiment, some pedestrians failed to notice which remarkable switch?
If a cough replaces a speech sound in a recorded sentence, listeners may believe they heard what?
An odd recording of “sine-wave speech” may initially sound like whistles. What can suddenly make the same recording intelligible?
Across many languages, people tend to pair the made-up word “kiki” with what sort of shape?
In a “choice blindness” experiment, people sometimes explained why they preferred a face photograph that had actually been what?
In a Reading study, which simple activity reduced reports of a catchy song repeating in participants’ minds?
In a 2003 case study, particular combinations of speech sounds consistently triggered which unusual sensation?
Which task is typically slowed by the Stroop effect?
After studying words such as bed, rest and awake, people in a classic memory experiment often “remembered” which word that had never appeared?
For people with the photic sneeze response, which unexpected event can trigger a sneeze?
In some people, stimulating the outer ear canal can unexpectedly trigger which reflex?
Identical twins can share virtually the same inherited DNA yet still differ in which familiar identification feature?
NC State researchers found thousands of microbial genetic types across samples from which small, often-overlooked body feature?
What can persist in a mother’s tissues for years after childbirth as a result of fetal microchimerism?
When researchers filmed knuckles cracking inside an MRI scanner, what appeared rapidly in the joint fluid?
A Brown sleep study found a “night watch” effect during the first night in unfamiliar surroundings. What was unusually uneven?
A gene variant associated with dry earwax also affects production of which surprisingly separate personal trait?
Inherited differences in odor detection help explain why some people cannot smell a distinctive urine odor after eating which vegetable?
Chemical growth records in baby teeth have helped researchers reconstruct which event from infancy?
After handshakes, hidden-camera research at Weizmann found an increase in what easily overlooked behavior?
In a sleep-onset study, even participants with amnesia who could not recall playing a game reported images from which game?
Under special laboratory conditions, people have perceived near-infrared light through what unusual retinal process?
In a detailed study of two people with six functional fingers per hand, brain scans found what for the extra finger?
The BrainPort system converts a camera image into patterns of electrical stimulation delivered to which body part?
In a laboratory illusion, a gently tapped hand began to feel harder and stiffer after researchers changed what?
When people located landmarks on their own hidden hands, the resulting mental maps tended to depict what distortion?
In an audio experiment, boosting high frequencies in the sound of hands rubbing together made the skin feel what?
In a Keele experiment comparing four utterances during a cold-water task, which increased pain tolerance?
The DishBrain experiment connected living neurons in a dish to a simplified version of which video game?
In an experiment with an itchy right forearm, scratching the left forearm reduced the itch most when participants saw what?
Repeatedly copying a familiar word can sometimes make it feel strangely unfamiliar. What is this opposite-of-déjà-vu experience called?
In a UCLA memory study, only one of 85 participants drew which familiar technology logo completely correctly?
A study of shared false visual memories examined people “remembering” which accessory on the usual Monopoly mascot?
In photo-preference research, people tended to prefer which version of their own face, unlike their friends’ usual preference?
People wearing a potentially embarrassing T-shirt in the “spotlight effect” experiments tended to overestimate what?
What unusual covering did University of Tokyo researchers attach to a robotic face that could smile?
In an experiment probing the limit of human vision, researchers generated pairs of photons. What happened to the partner of the photon sent toward the eye?
To create the intensely saturated color perception called “olo,” Berkeley’s Oz system selectively stimulated what?
A study of people newly able to see after congenital blindness tested whether they could immediately identify by sight objects known by what other sense?
The tiny moving lights known as “blue-sky sprites” arise from which cells moving through vessels in the eye?
When the body metabolizes stored fat, most of that fat’s mass eventually leaves by which route?
In developmental experiments, some young children thought they could hide themselves merely by concealing what?
After practice stepping onto a moving platform, participants were explicitly told it had stopped. What happened on their first step onto it?
In the autokinetic illusion, a single dim light in an otherwise dark room seems to do what while actually staying still?
A mouse study investigating why tattoos persist found that replacement immune cells did what with pigment released by older cells?
Using synchrotron analysis, researchers found that some particles from human tattoos had traveled beyond the skin to where?
Some skin pigmentation patterns follow the curved lines of Blaschko. These patterns can reveal what hidden biological patchwork?
Rapidly cycling through aligned photographs of ordinary faces can make them appear like what, despite leaving the photos unedited?
Tiny experimental Anthrobots were made from adult human cells normally found in which lining?
A prototype fingertip fuel cell developed at UC San Diego generated electricity while its wearer slept by harvesting what?
In the experimental BrainNet system, what did a receiver perceive when a teammate sent a “rotate the block” instruction through the brain interface?
In thermal-taste experiments, warming a previously cooled tongue tip can produce which taste even without sugar?
Syncytin, a protein that helps human placental cells fuse, was adapted during evolution from what source?
The antibiotic compound lugdunin was discovered in bacteria living in which surprisingly ordinary human location?
A study of 60 French and German newborns found a difference in their cries that echoed the melody of their surroundings. Which sound feature differed?
In research in the Australian Aboriginal community of Pormpuraaw, people often arranged chronological pictures according to what reference?
A Russian-English color experiment explored a linguistic boundary between which two colors that English usually groups under one basic color name?
In a sleep-learning experiment, tones were paired with pleasant or unpleasant odors. What did participants later do when the tones played without any odor?
The faint bow-tie pattern called Haidinger’s brushes reveals that human eyes can detect which property of light?
An EPFL robotic experiment created a spooky feeling by introducing a mismatch between a participant’s movement and touch on their back. What did some participants sense?
Research on developing fingerprints found that their ridges follow a shortened version of the developmental program for what other skin structure?
In a 2023 experiment, men exposed to women’s emotional tears showed less of which behavior during a competitive laboratory game?
After using a mechanical grabber, participants in a body-perception experiment judged touches at their elbow and fingertip as if their arm had become what?
In the Pulfrich illusion, darkening the view through one eye can make a pendulum swinging side to side appear to follow what path?
A 2021 Stanford brain-interface study produced on-screen text while a participant imagined performing which action?
The memory-related protein Arc can assemble into tiny virus-like packages. What cargo did researchers find these packages could carry between laboratory-grown neurons?
A University of Tokyo two-legged robot reported in 2024 moved using electrically stimulated pieces of what?
In a small study of two people with severe amnesia, what happened when another meal was offered shortly after one they had forgotten eating?
In a study of 32 Turkish-English bilinguals, taboo words produced a stronger skin-conductance response when presented in which language?
In an experiment involving a simulated walk through rooms, when did recognition memory start to worsen around a doorway?
In a 2025 study, fingertips were soaked on separate occasions and their wrinkles compared. What did the researchers find about the wrinkle patterns?
Participants in a frightening free-fall experiment remembered their fall as unusually long. What did a flashing-digit test reveal about their vision during the fall?
In research on why a return journey can feel shorter, what happened when cyclists returned by a different but equally long route?
In a human brain-recording study, what weakened when participants switched from breathing through the nose to breathing through the mouth?
Researchers made an experimental yarn for weaving tissue-engineering materials from sheets of what?
University of Cape Town researchers grew experimental bricks at room temperature using sand, bacteria, and which human waste product?
A Harvard biohybrid fish described in 2022 swam using human stem-cell-derived cells of which type?
Wind-tunnel experiments with model eyelashes found that excessively long lashes could have what surprising effect?
Patients with severe memory impairment could improve at which task despite poor recollection of the practice sessions?
In experiments using a computerized balloon-risk game, which basic taste was associated with more risk-taking?
People listening attentively to the same story can show correlated fluctuations in which bodily measure, even without interacting?
When people watched the same short video stories, their blinks often synchronized at which moments?
Human egg cells activated in laboratory experiments released a burst of which metal, visualized with fluorescent probes?
Duke researchers found that shifting your eyes while keeping your head still also produces tiny movements in which structures?
A fingertip-inspired sensor suggested that fingerprint ridges help fine-texture perception by selecting and amplifying what?
During a guided museum-tour study, photographing an entire object was followed by what result compared with simply observing it?
In a Yale experiment, adding logically irrelevant information from which field made poor psychological explanations more satisfying to nonexperts?
Bone has a tiny piezoelectric response: mechanical and electrical effects are coupled. Which major bone component is a principal contributor?
X-rays overturned an early death-date claim for the Mütter Museum’s “Soap Lady” by revealing which hidden evidence?
A study of people blind from birth found that, when speaking to another blind person, they did what with their hand gestures?
In experiments on unfamiliar sayings, which wording change made a statement seem more accurate without changing its basic meaning?
In a tactile illusion, moving two parallel metal wires between the palms can make people feel they are touching what kind of surface?
Research into an old art-conservation technique identified an enzyme in which bodily fluid as an effective cleaning agent?
Worcester Polytechnic Institute researchers grew beating human heart cells on the stripped-down framework of which vegetable?
In a 2015 study, repeated false statements gained credibility even when participants had what?
A tongue-in-cheek randomized trial found no injury benefit from parachutes versus empty backpacks. What crucial detail explains the result?
Four adults in a 2008 study could hear something while watching silent flashes or visual motion. What gave them an advantage on a visual rhythm task?
In the magician’s Criss-Cross force, a spectator freely chooses where to cut a deck. Which card is ultimately presented as their selection?
